title_en: From Generalist to Specialist at Columbia's Endowment – Erlina Yeo Terwelp (EP.520)
title_zh: 从通才到专才：Columbia 捐赠基金的私募版图 – Erlina Yeo Terwelp（EP.520）
subtitle_zh: Columbia 捐赠基金私募主管 Erlina Yeo Terwelp 谈管理人选择、组合构建，以及从通才到专才的蜕变。
description: From Generalist to Specialist at Columbia's Endowment – Erlina Yeo Terwelp (EP.520)

turns.en: I don't think there is huge difference in the fundamentals of what you're looking at between a business and a manager. All managers need to look at their firms as businesses as well.
turns.zh: 我不认为在一家企业和一位管理人之间，你们所考察的基本面有多大差别。所有管理人都需要把自己的机构当成一门生意来看待。

turns.en: Bet rock of what we did as a generalist was that every investment opportunity was evaluated in its cleanest forms, which was what's equity beta, what's the liquidity and what's the cost of that and what's its leverage.
turns.zh: 我们作为通才（generalist）时打下的根基在于：每一个投资机会都会在最纯粹的形式下被评估，也就是它的股票贝塔（equity beta）是多少、流动性如何、成本是多少、杠杆又是多少。

turns.en: Not necessarily, do we want an India VC manager or do we want a X type of manager? There was very little bucket filling. It was a bottom sub, first principles of what an investment was.
turns.zh: 而不是说，我们要不要一个印度的 VC 管理人，或者要不要某一类型的管理人。几乎没有凑数式的填桶。它是自下而上、从一笔投资的第一性原理出发的。

turns.en: I belong to the school where I believe that there's probably five things unique to every investment that will make or break the deal or make or break the returns.
turns.zh: 我信奉这样一种观点：每一笔投资大概都有五件独特的东西，会决定这笔交易成败，或者决定回报好坏。

turns.en: We try to get to those questions in a five-page error. I'm Ted Sides and this is Capital Allocators. The CIOs of the largest pools of capital have jobs that require broad skill sets.
turns.zh: 我们试图在五页备忘录（five-pager）里问到这些问题。我是 Ted Seides，这里是 Capital Allocators。那些最大资金池的 CIO，他们的工作需要广博的技能组合。

turns.en: They cover the world across asset classes and strategies, determine portfolio construction and decide what goes into their portfolio. They're also leaders, managing people in an investment office, working with a board and taking care of all their stakeholders, whether students, grantees, pensioners, family members, insured recipients or sovereign states.
turns.zh: 他们横跨各类资产和策略看遍全球，决定组合构建，决定什么进入他们的组合。他们也是领导者，管理投资办公室的人，与董事会合作，照顾好所有利益相关方——无论学生、受助者、养老金领取者、家族成员、被保险人，还是主权国家。

turns.en: It's a complex role that involves far more than just investing. But they don't do it alone. Behind every successful CIO is a talented team who focuses most, if not all of their time, on investing.
turns.zh: 这是一个复杂的角色，远不止投资本身。但他们并非孤军奋战。每一位成功的 CIO 背后，都有一支把大部分、乃至全部时间专注在投资上的优秀团队。

turns.en: We spend time with many of these senior decision makers at our summits and find their closest to the action and deeply insightful about investment opportunities and the investment process.
turns.zh: 我们在峰会上会与许多这样的高层决策者相处，发现他们最贴近一线，对投资机会和投资流程有着深刻的洞见。

turns.en: This miniseries, senior decision makers, features conversations with investors that have not yet ascended to the CIO seat. These professionals are the primary driver of decisions that lead new ideas into a portfolio or exits from a manager's strategy and are at a fascinating point in their career.
turns.zh: 这个名为'高层决策者'（senior decision makers）的迷你系列，收录的是那些尚未坐上 CIO 位置的投资人的对话。这些专业人士是推动决策的主要力量——把新理念引入组合，或退出某位管理人的策略——正处在职业生涯中一个引人入胜的阶段。

turns.en: My partner and the CEO of capital allocators Hank Sturmack will take the mic and lead an exploration of the investment thinking and role of senior decision makers.
turns.zh: 我的搭档、Capital Allocators 的 CEO Hank Sturmack 会接过话筒，带大家探索高层决策者的投资思考与角色。

turns.en: Our next guest on the senior decision maker series is Erlina Yo Turwell, a managing director at Columbia Investment Management Company, where she oversees the endowment's private markets portfolio.
turns.zh: 我们'高层决策者'系列的下一位嘉宾是 Erlina Yeo Terwelp，她是 Columbia Investment Management Company 的董事总经理（managing director），负责监督这所大学的捐赠基金（endowment）的私募市场组合。

turns.en: Erlina's path spans investment banking, private equity, growth equity, and family office investing before she joined Columbia nearly a decade ago.
turns.zh: Erlina 的职业路径横跨投行、私募股权、成长型股权和家族办公室投资，之后她在近十年前加入了 Columbia。

turns.en: Our conversation covers her evolution as an allocator, how she thinks about manager selection and portfolio construction, the growing role of leadership and team development in her seat, and her perspectives on generalists versus specialist team models after working within both.
turns.zh: 我们的对话涵盖她作为配置者的成长、她如何看待管理人选择与组合构建、她在位上领导力与团队培养日益重要的角色，以及她先后在通才和专才团队模式内工作之后，对这两者的看法。

turns.en: Erlina is candid, thoughtful, and very funny, with a deep commitment to intellectual honesty and openness to changing her mind and a willingness to continually put herself in situations that force her to grow.
turns.zh: Erlina 坦诚、深思熟虑，而且非常风趣，对智识诚实有坚定的承诺，乐于改变自己的想法，并愿意不断把自己放进那种逼她成长的情境里。

turns.en: Before we get to the interview, AI voice cloning has gotten scary good. Apparently, mine has too. I've hosted the first few interviews in our new senior decision maker series, and you're about to hear the next.
turns.zh: 在进入访谈之前，AI 语音克隆已经可怕地逼真了。看来我的也是。我主持了我们新推出的'高层决策者'系列的前几期访谈，你马上要听到的是下一期。

turns.en: The funny part is, I've now had multiple people tell me they had no idea it was me behind the mic. They thought they were listening to Ted the entire time.
turns.zh: 有趣的是，已经有好几个人告诉我，他们完全没料到话筒后面的人是我。他们一直以为自己在听 Ted 的节目。

turns.en: Recently, I was on a call, and someone told me how much they liked Ted's conversation with Nick Sisko at Trinity Wall Street. I interviewed Nick.
turns.zh: 最近我在一个电话上，有人告诉我他们有多喜欢 Ted 与 Nick Sisko 在 Trinity Wall Street 的那期对话。其实是我采的 Nick。

turns.en: I didn't have the heart to correct them. While AI keeps improving, apparently my Ted voice is right there with it. So tell your colleagues about the latest senior decision maker episode.
turns.zh: 我不忍心纠正他们。AI 一直在进步，显然我的'Ted 声音'也紧跟其后。所以请把你的同事也介绍来听最新一期'高层决策者'。

turns.en: No need to tell them who's hosting. Let them decide if it's me, Ted, or AI. Thanks so much for spreading the word. Capital Allocators is brought to you by Alpha Sense.
turns.zh: 不用告诉他们是谁在主持。让他们自己去猜，是我、是 Ted，还是 AI。非常感谢你们的口耳相传。Capital Allocators 由 AlphaSense 呈现。

turns.en: Every allocator sits at their desk for hours preparing the work around investment decisions, getting up to speed on a new theme, prepping for the next investment committee meeting, and tracking what changes across an entire portfolio.
turns.zh: 每位配置者都会在桌前坐上几个小时，为投资决策做准备：熟悉一个新主题，为下一次投资委员会会议做准备，跟踪整个组合里发生了哪些变化。

turns.en: Alpha Sense just launched something built to help. It's called Super Analyst, an always-on agent that works like a power user on your behalf.
turns.zh: AlphaSense 刚刚推出了一款为此而生的产品，叫 Super Analyst，一个随时在线的 agent，像一位资深用户一样替你工作。

turns.en: It draws on over 500 million premium sources, including broker research, expert transcripts, city filings, and earnings calls, and keeps working long after you've gone home for the day.
turns.zh: 它调用超过 5 亿份优质信源，包括卖方研究、专家纪要、公司备案文件和财报电话会，在你下班回家很久之后仍在继续工作。

turns.en: Point Super Analyst at a theme, company, or market, and it learns the coverage universe so you can easily turn new insights into the briefs, models, and memos you'd otherwise build by hand.
turns.zh: 把 Super Analyst 指向一个主题、公司或市场，它就会学习整个覆盖域，让你轻松把新洞察变成你原本要手动撰写的简报、模型和备忘录。

turns.en: It was designed to work like an extension of your team, so it remembers your projects, follows your templates and processes, and links every output to its source so you can see where each conclusion came from.
turns.zh: 它的设计初衷是像团队的延伸一样工作——它记住你的项目，遵循你的模板和流程，并把每一个产出链接到它的来源，让你看清每个结论从何而来。

turns.en: The best way to judge its quality is to give it a whirl. Pick the research task on your desk before your next committee meeting and hand it to Super Analyst.
turns.zh: 评判它质量的最佳方式就是亲自试一试。在下一次委员会会议之前，挑一件摊在你桌上的研究任务，交给 Super Analyst。

turns.zh: 前往 alpha-sense.com/capital 开始免费试用，看看它为你准备好了什么。Capital Allocators 也由 Ridgeline 呈现——一个为那些正在重新思考工作方式的机构打造的投资管理平台。

turns.zh: 你坐在桌前，看着一条代表贵机构增长的折线图。线在横着走，是线性增长，而你确切知道原因：你的运营带宽受限，低到太久了，简直像是做生意的成本。

turns.zh: Ridgeline 就是为了改变这条线的轨迹而生，成为那个拐点，用你现有的团队把增长从渐进推向加速。

turns.en: Ridgeline is the only AI-native investment management platform that brings together the front, middle, and back office with one set of data and powerful AI agents that automate away operational drudgery so your talent can shift from managing old technology to materializing new ideas.
turns.zh: Ridgeline 是唯一一个 AI 原生的投资管理平台，把前台、中台、后台用同一套数据和强大的 AI agent 整合在一起，把运营琐事自动化掉，让你的团队从维护旧技术转向把新想法变为现实。

turns.zh: Ridgeline 帮助资产与财富管理机构理解并改善其增长轨迹。要看看你的机构与 16,000 家同行相比如何，请访问 ridgeline.ai/trajectory。

turns.zh: 如果你提交过 Form ADV，你的机构就已经在里面了。然后就与 Ridgeline 聊聊，如何用现有团队做得更多。Capital Allocators 也由 Juniper Square 呈现——那个被领先私募市场 GP 信赖的运营合作伙伴。

turns.zh: 节目里反复出现的一个主题是：与 LP 建立最稳固、最持久关系的 GP，是那些既有强劲回报、又有强劲运营的机构。

turns.zh: AI 提高了运营的分量，而把 Juniper Square 作为你的运营伙伴，能帮助确保你的数据有条理、准确、可取用，从而释放运营层面的 alpha。

turns.en: That's why thousands of GPs trust Juniper Square. Learn more at junipersquare.com slash capital allocators. Please enjoy the next conversation in our Senior Decision Maker series with Erlina Yo Terwell.
turns.zh: 这正是成千上万 GP 信赖 Juniper Square 的原因。更多信息请访问 junipersquare.com/capital-allocators。请欣赏我们'高层决策者'系列的下一段对话，嘉宾是 Erlina Yeo Terwelp。

turns.en: Erlina, thanks so much for doing this. Thank you for having me. I want to start with a question that we use as an icebreaker at some of our summits.
turns.zh: Erlina，非常感谢你来做这期节目。谢谢邀请。我想先用一个我们在一些峰会上当作破冰的问题来开始。

turns.en: Tell us where you grew up and how that upbringing has informed who you are today. I grew up in Singapore. I spent 18 years of my life in Singapore.
turns.zh: 告诉我们你在哪里长大，那样的成长环境如何塑造了今天的你。我在新加坡长大，我人生最初的 18 年都在新加坡度过。

turns.en: My father was a commodities trader. He did that for more than three decades. My mom has a doctorate in organizational behavior, ran her own consulting firm.
turns.zh: 我父亲是一名大宗商品交易员，做了三十多年。我妈妈有组织行为学的博士学位，经营过自己的咨询公司。

turns.en: When people asked me about my upbringing, it was such a yin and yang. My dad was tactical, direct, and brought everything you would expect the trader to be.
turns.zh: 当别人问起我的成长环境时，那真的是阴阳两极。我父亲偏战术、直接，带着你对一个交易员的全部预期。

turns.en: My mom, who is strategic and psychoanalyzes everybody that she knows, including her three kids, grew up knowing my mayor's breaks, knowing where I stood.
turns.zh: 我妈妈则偏战略，会去精神分析她认识的每一个人——包括她的三个孩子——我在了解她的重大抉择、知道她站在什么位置的氛围里长大。

turns.en: How does that yin and yang come through today at this stage of your life and professional career? This job brought it together for me. You have two voices in your head and sometimes contradictory, this long-term, short-term.
turns.zh: 那种阴阳两极，在你今天这个人生和职业阶段是如何体现的？这份工作把它们为我合在了一起。你脑子里有两个声音，有时还互相矛盾：一个看长期，一个看短期。

turns.en: How do I tell somebody something directly? How do I couch it in a way that they understand and empathetically? In this job specifically, there is a lot of dynamic decisions that you have to make around different investment opportunities, around trade-offs, around risk and return profiles.
turns.zh: 我要怎么直接地告诉某人一件事？怎么把它包裹成对方能理解、又有同理心的方式？具体到这份工作，你要围绕不同的投资机会、围绕取舍、围绕风险收益特征做大量动态决策。

turns.en: My dad's side of things where he thinks a lot in, what do you buy something for? What is it worth? Can you sell it? What's the risk profile around that?
turns.zh: 我父亲那一面，他很擅长这样思考：你花多少钱买一样东西？它值多少？你能卖得掉吗？围绕它的风险特征是什么？

turns.en: That's always been part of my DNA that comes deeply for me in this particular job. My mom's side of things is about people. The people's side of things is such an important part of this business.
turns.zh: 那一直是我 DNA 的一部分，在这份特定的工作里对我来说来得很自然。我妈妈那一面是关于人的。而关于人的那一面，是这个行业里如此重要的一部分。

turns.en: Everything that we see is human capital. Understanding both sides, having things brought up in this environment was interesting for me. What was your entry into the investment business?
turns.zh: 我们看到的一切都是人力资本。在这样一个环境里长大、同时理解这两面，对我来说很有意思。那你是怎么进入投资行业的？

turns.en: From a very young age, I was introduced to the idea of business and trading because of what my dad did. He was a fan of Warren Buffett. There were books lying around the house about investing.
turns.zh: 我很小就因为我父亲做的事接触到了商业和交易的概念。他是 Warren Buffett 的粉丝，家里到处放着关于投资的书。

turns.en: When I was in high school, economics was by far my favorite topic. It was the arts and science. It's about psychology as much as it is about business and understanding microeconomics.
turns.zh: 高中的时候，经济学是我最喜欢的科目，远超过其他。它既是文科也是理科——它关乎心理学，也同样关乎商业和理解微观经济学。

turns.en: When I first picked up an investing book and started learning about economics, I thought it was such a great combination of everything that I loved, which was literature, math, history.
turns.zh: 当我第一次拿起一本投资的书、开始学习经济学时，我觉得它把我热爱的东西——文学、数学、历史——结合得那么妙。

turns.en: I applied early to Columbia. It was the one university that I wanted to go to because of its proximity to New York and the finance industry.
turns.zh: 我提前申请（early application）了 Columbia。它是唯一我想去的大学，因为它邻近纽约和金融行业。

turns.en: I just loved the Renaissance man-woman type of education where you got to learn a lot of different things about everything. My first foray into the investment world was my first job at investment banking at City, but started way before that.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢那种文艺复兴式的通才教育，让你对万事万物都能学到很多不同的东西。我涉足投资世界的第一份工作是在 Citi 做投行的投资银行业务，但那之前早就开始了。

turns.en: I had a big curiosity around that industry. What was the path from City? I graduated in 2006. 2006 was a great year. We were doing the biggest LBO deals that were out there.
turns.zh: 我对那个行业有强烈的好奇。从 Citi 起步的路径是怎样的？我 2006 年毕业。2006 年是很好的一年，我们在做市场上最大的 LBO（杠杆收购）交易。

turns.en: I was in a consumer group. I worked on things like the KKR Dollar General LBO and everyone was so happy. It was a new foray moment. It was an interesting contrast because the next year, being in banking and particularly city group, was an interesting place to be.
turns.zh: 我在消费组。我参与过像 KKR 收购 Dollar General 那样的 LBO，大家都很开心，那是一个新纪元般的时刻。有趣的对比是，接下来一年，身处银行业、尤其是 Citi 组，是个很有意思的地方。

turns.en: It was a very early career trauma, the top of the top. Then the next year, you get the rug pulled out from under. It introduced a lot of paranoia.
turns.zh: 那是一段非常早期的职业创伤——巅峰中的巅峰。然后第二年，地毯就从你脚下被抽走了。它带来了很多偏执。

turns.en: I decided to go work at Cadetin, which was at that time a lower-middle market firm specializing in consumer. Cadetin was an exceptional place.
turns.zh: 我决定去 Camden 工作，那时它是一家专注消费的中低端市场机构。Camden 是个非凡的地方。

turns.en: I still have great mentors from there. They were different in the sense that early on, they were operationally focused. I worked a ton with the CEOs and CFOs of our portfolio companies.
turns.zh: 我在那里至今仍有很好的导师。他们的不同之处在于，很早就以运营为重。我和我们组合公司的 CEO、CFO 们一起做了大量工作。

turns.en: From there, I went to business school for a couple of years, worked for a quick stint at a fund one growth equity shop before I moved to Houston.
turns.zh: 从那之后，我读了一段时间商学院，在一家成长型股权机构短暂工作过，然后搬到了休斯顿。

turns.en: I moved to Houston for the oldest story known to mankind, which is love. My husband, who was then my fiance, went to medical school a little later in life.
turns.zh: 我搬到休斯顿是为了人类有史以来最古老的那个故事——爱情。我先生——那时还是我未婚夫——较晚才去上医学院。

turns.en: I went to Houston for four years. At that time, there was no working remote, there was no zooms. Then I was relatively young and decided to just move to Houston, not knowing that many people.
turns.zh: 我在休斯顿待了四年。那时候没有远程办公，也没有 Zoom。那时我还相对年轻，就决定直接搬到休斯顿，认识的人没几个。

turns.en: I had to very sadly quit my job. When I got to Houston, I cold-called a ton of people, eventually found a place at a family office there. When I got to the family office, I was able to consider optionality there.
turns.zh: 我很遗憾不得不辞掉工作。到了休斯顿后，我打了大量陌生电话（cold call），最终在当地一家家族办公室找到了一席之地。到了那家家族办公室，我得以在那里考量可选性（optionality）。

turns.en: They asked me to step in as the interim CFO for a company of one of the families for about six months. It was a bit of a turnaround situation.
turns.zh: 他们让我去其中一位家族成员的公司里临时担任 CFO 大约六个月。那是一个有点 turnaround（困境反转）意味的局面。

turns.en: I went in and did all the things that Camden taught me around operations, KPIs, thought about the things that they could do to drive sales or increase margins.
turns.zh: 我进去后做了所有 Camden 教我的那些事——围绕运营、KPI，思考他们可以采取哪些举措来拉动销售或提升利润率。

turns.en: We ended up putting in a new president. I was able to apply a playbook to a company that was further away from the New York private equity scene.
turns.zh: 我们最终换上了一位新总裁。我得以把一套打法应用到一家离纽约私募股权圈更远的公司上。

turns.en: Concurrently, I was asked to take a look at the alternatives portfolio as well, which at that time included all of the above asset classes. We did a lot of hedge funds, we did a lot of loan only.
turns.zh: 与此同时，他们也让我去看另类投资（alternatives）组合，那里面涵盖了上面所有资产类别。我们做了很多对冲基金，也做了很多 loan-only（纯贷款）策略。

turns.en: We also were starting the private side of things. There was a lot of directs down there, so I worked primarily on directs with direct companies on Navisti and real estate side.
turns.zh: 我们也开始做私募那一侧。那里有很多直接投资（directs），所以我主要和 Navisti 以及房地产那一侧的直接投资、直接公司打交道。

turns.en: Then we did a couple of funds. It was almost a direct flip of what I had been doing before because I was looking at a lot of different types of investments and a much bigger scale than I had before.
turns.zh: 然后我们做了几只基金。那几乎是我之前工作的一种直接翻版，因为我看的投资类型多得多、规模也比以前大得多。

turns.en: That's when I fell in love with the LP world. I thought it was so fascinating. What was fascinating about it? You can walk into your office every day and think the world's your oyster.
turns.zh: 就在那时我爱上了 LP 的世界，觉得它太迷人了。它迷人在哪里？你可以每天走进办公室，觉得整个世界都是你的牡蛎。

turns.en: How do you make money with so many different types of strategies and different geographies and different sectors? It's a different proposition than walking into your office every day and having a mandate where you had to buy a consumer company that was excised and that did ex things.
turns.zh: 在这么多不同的策略、不同的地域、不同的行业里，你怎么赚钱？这和每天走进办公室、却有一个限定任务——你得去买一家被剥离的、做某类业务的消费公司——完全是两回事。

turns.en: The brightness of the opportunity set was fascinating. I've met such interesting people and some of the best minds in financial industry, amazing educational experience for someone who's curious.
turns.zh: 机会集的广度令人着迷。我遇到过这么多有趣的人、金融行业里一些最好的头脑，对一个好奇心重的人来说，那是绝妙的学习经历。

turns.en: What was the transition from the family office world to the endowment world? I moved back to New York after four years in Houston, did the same thing where I co-called a bunch of people.
turns.zh: 那从家族办公室世界转到捐赠基金世界又是怎么回事？我在休斯顿待了四年后搬回纽约，又做了同样的事——打了一堆陌生电话。

turns.en: My response rate was maybe 10%. You could count them with your fingers. Funnily enough, three of the people who responded to me were Peter Holland and Tim Donahue, who at that time led the Colombian Dowman.
turns.zh: 我的回复率大概只有 10%，一只手都能数得过来。有意思的是，回复我的三个人里有 Peter Holland 和 Tim Donahue，他们当时正执掌 Columbia 的捐赠基金。

turns.en: I said, why don't you come on in and we'll chat and see if there's an opportunity here. The other person who responded to me was Kim Lu. I met her early on in my career.
turns.zh: 他们说，你何不过来我们聊聊，看看这里有没有机会。另一个回复我的人是 Kim Lu，我在职业生涯早期就认识她。

turns.en: I thought it was so great that she responded and gave me a 30-minute slot on my calendar. Why do you think Tim, Peter and Kim replied to your cold calls?
turns.zh: 她居然回复了、还在我日历上给了我 30 分钟，我觉得特别好。你觉得为什么 Tim、Peter 和 Kim 会回复你的陌生电话？

turns.en: When I wrote to them, I said, here's my background. This is why I'm interested in your organization. For Colombia, it was an easy one. I had gone there.
turns.zh: 我写给他们时，会说：这是我的背景，这就是我对你所在机构感兴趣的原因。对 Columbia 来说，这很容易——我去过那里。

turns.en: Education was super important to me. My parents were both scholarship holders. I wrote about why the institution was important to me as well.
turns.zh: 教育对我极其重要，我父母都是拿奖学金出来的。我也写了为什么这所学校对我重要。

turns.en: They did the same for Kim. She and I had both gone to the same business school. I tried to leverage that as well. I always couched this an opportunity to connect and learn, which is valuable.
turns.zh: 对 Kim 我也是这么写的。她和我上的是同一所商学院，我也试着借力这一点。我总是把它包装成一次建立联系和学习的机会——那是有价值的。

turns.en: I've been the two times that I've had to switch jobs by cold calling. I have met still many people that I have been so intrigued by and have continued to be friends of the industry throughout the whole time.
turns.zh: 我靠打陌生电话换过两次工作。我结识了很多人，对他们一直很好奇，并且在整个过程中一直保持朋友关系。

turns.en: I never thought of any of those opportunities as a transactional one. It was more, I value what your organization does. I value what your position is.
turns.zh: 我从没把那些机会当成一笔交易性的事。更多的是一种：我看重你所在机构做的事，我看重你所处的位置。

turns.en: If you find me interesting as a person for your group, that's great. What was the process of Tim and Peter answering a cold call to then you joining the endowment?
turns.zh: 如果你作为一个人对我的团队有意思，那很好。那从 Tim 和 Peter 回复一个陌生电话，到你最终加入捐赠基金，中间是个什么过程？

turns.en: I was applying for the position and I had already been filled, which I did not at that time know. When they responded, they said, hopefully we could chat, come by the office.
turns.zh: 我当时在应聘那个职位，但那个职位其实已经被人占了，只是那时候我不知道。他们回复时说，希望我们能聊聊，来办公室坐坐。

turns.en: Back then, my resume was off-chilter. It wasn't a standard endowment resume. I had been in a lot of different places. Tim and Peter valued that.
turns.zh: 那时候我的简历很不主流，不是一份标准的捐赠基金简历。我在很多地方待过。Tim 和 Peter 很看重这一点。

turns.en: At that time, Columbia had a lot of people who had come from a lot of different places as well. I went through an entire interview process and met with them 10 times and I was living in Houston then, so I would have to fly back and forth to do that.
turns.zh: 那时 Columbia 也有很多来自五湖四海的人。我走完了整个面试流程，和他们见了 10 次面，而我当时住在休斯顿，所以得飞来飞去。

turns.en: Thankfully, I joined Columbia about nine years ago. What initially were your responsibilities? What was the endowment like back then? Nine years ago, I joined as a generalist.
turns.zh: 好在，我大约九年前加入了 Columbia。你最初负责哪些事？那时候的捐赠基金是什么样？九年前，我是以通才身份加入的。

turns.en: I worked on a lot of different asset classes. If I were to think about my split, it would probably be 50% hedge funds, only 50% private equity and niche strategies.
turns.zh: 我做过很多不同的资产类别。如果要说我的精力分配，大概是 50% 对冲基金，另外 50% 私募股权和细分策略。

turns.en: I was particularly interested in that area. The manager selection piece was the biggest emphasis there. There was a lot of focus on making sure that that manager could deliver alpha.
turns.zh: 我特别对那一领域感兴趣。管理人选择是那里最大的重点。我们非常关注确保那位管理人能交付 alpha。

turns.en: We spent a lot of time in manager selection. Two of the things that Columbia was good at was data. We've always had a data team. I learned a lot from the way it was structured.
turns.zh: 我们在管理人选择上花了很多时间。Columbia 擅长的两件事之一是数据。我们一直有一个数据团队，我从它的组织方式里学到了很多。

turns.en: We had a strategic asset allocation in that we knew what it was, but it was managed differently from the traditional endowment. We managed it through risk factor allocation, something that is more similar to today's total portfolio approach.
turns.zh: 我们有一套战略资产配置——我们知道它是什么——但它的管理方式不同于传统捐赠基金。我们通过风险因子配置（risk factor allocation）来管理，更接近今天的总组合方法（total portfolio approach，TPA）。

turns.en: That was different because it was not as simple to understand. It took a lot to understand the depths of how do you roll everything up so that you can understand things with the overlay that you had created.
turns.zh: 那之所以不同，是因为它没那么容易理解。要花很大力气才能理解其中的深度——你怎么把一切汇总上去，从而带着你所搭建的叠加层（overlay）去理解各种东西。

turns.en: Those two things, being a generalist and approaching the portfolio allocation from a different way than it traditionally did, was two of the biggest learnings for me.
turns.zh: 这两件事——做通才，以及用不同于传统的方式去做组合配置——是我最大的两项收获。

turns.en: I want to tap into some of those in particular. The first one you mentioned was just the emphasis on manager selection. With your background, even at the family office, you said only a portion of your time was spent with external funds, where there was a lot of direct investments.
turns.zh: 我想深入其中几点。你提到的第一点就是对管理人选择的强调。以你的背景——即便在家族办公室，你也说只有部分时间花在外部的基金上，因为那里有大量直接投资。

turns.en: You spent time as a CFO of an operating business. When you initially joined, what were some of the skills and new routines and muscles that you needed to build related to manager selection that may be more common and easy for you nine years in?
turns.zh: 你也当过一家经营性公司的 CFO。当你刚加入时，围绕管理人选择，你需要培养哪些技能、新的习惯和'肌肉'——而这些到你已做了九年时可能变得更常见、更容易？

turns.en: I had developed some of that at the family office already, because I don't think there is huge difference in the fundamentals of what you're looking at between a business and a manager.
turns.zh: 我在家族办公室已经发展了其中一些，因为我不认为在一家企业和一位管理人之间，你所考察的基本面有多大差别。

turns.en: You need to look at the positioning and the way that they're in, whether they're both. All these things apply equally to a business as it does to a manager.
turns.zh: 你需要看定位，看他们切入的方式——所有这些对一家企业和对一位管理人同样适用。

turns.en: All managers need to look at their firms as businesses as well. Thinking about the edge positioning, their modes, on the other side, the people that make up the executive team there, whether it's a couple of GPs or a solo GP, that's not that different from looking at a company where you're looking at a CEO and their team.
turns.zh: 所有管理人都需要把自己的机构当成一门生意来看待。想想 edge 定位、他们的模式，另一方面是组成执行团队的那些人——不管是两位 GP 还是单一 GP——这和看一家公司、看一位 CEO 和他们的团队并没有太大不同。

turns.en: It's their ability to inspire people, to hire talent, to execute, to think about what the next strategic goals are. All those things are similar between a business and a manager.
turns.zh: 是他们激励人、招募人才、执行的能力，是思考下一个战略目标是什么。所有这些在企业和管理人之间都是相似的。

turns.en: From an investment perspective, it wasn't that different from a network perspective. It was different, because when you are a direct investor, you are looking for companies all day.
turns.zh: 从投资的视角看，差别没那么大；但从网络的视角看就不同了，因为当你做直接投资人时，你整天都在找公司。

turns.en: You're not necessarily meeting with funds. You don't really know what's going on, especially when you're not the person who is running the fund.
turns.zh: 你不见得在见基金。你其实不知道行业里在发生什么，尤其是当你自己不是那个管理基金的人时。

turns.en: You don't probably think about your competitors that much, unless they are across the auction table from you. The emphasis on the network, the LP network, the GP network, was something that I had to build out in those early days.
turns.zh: 你可能不会太多地考虑你的竞争对手，除非他们就在竞价桌的另一端。对网络的强调——LP 网络、GP 网络——是我在早期需要搭建起来的东西。

turns.en: The portfolio construction and allocation piece has also been something that is different. When you think about a direct deal, you are thinking about it singularly and also in the context of maybe a 12-feel portfolio within your buyout fund.
turns.zh: 组合构建与配置这一块也有所不同。当你看一笔直接交易时，你是孤立地看它，也许也放在你收购基金内一个约 12 笔投资的组合里来看。

turns.en: Portfolio construction of funds is different. On top of that, you have an asset allocation decision and risk management decisions that you have to make that are very different.
turns.zh: 基金的组合构建是不同的。而在此之上，你还要做资产配置决策和风险管理决策，那又完全不同。

turns.en: All those things were my biggest learning curves. The other piece you mentioned was around the data component, how you were leveraging risk factors and what we might know as TPA these days.
turns.zh: 所有这些都是我最大的学习曲线。你提到的另一块是关于数据——你们怎么利用风险因子，以及我们如今所说的 TPA。

turns.en: Nine years ago, that wasn't common vernacular in an institutional portfolio, at least not all. What was it that Columbia and you were doing back then that was different than a typical endowment approach to investing?
turns.zh: 九年前，在一个机构组合里，那还不是通行的说法，至少不全是。当时 Columbia 和你在做什么，区别于典型捐赠基金的投资方式？

turns.en: It was less common back then to manage to an equity beta or a range as more of a form of dynamic risk management. That's what TPA is bringing into the system.
turns.zh: 那时候，把组合管理到某个股票贝塔或一个区间、作为一种动态风险管理，还不太常见。那正是 TPA 带进体系里的东西。

turns.en: A lot of people may not have had the ability or the need to go look at what tilts they had and what risk factors they were exposed to, particularly on a public site.
turns.zh: 很多人或许没有能力、也没有需求去查看自己有哪些倾斜（tilt）、暴露在哪些风险因子上，尤其是在公开市场那一侧。

turns.en: It was a manage a lot like a hedge fund that emphasis on knowing all those pieces of data allowed us to move quickly, allowed us to see a lot of things, particularly on a public site.
turns.zh: 它管理起来很像一家对冲基金——那种对掌握所有这些数据片段的强调，让我们能快速行动，看到很多东西，尤其是在公开市场那一侧。

turns.en: Privates is a different animal. TPA is difficult to do with some private markets and some private asset classes. That rock of what we did as a generalist was that every investment opportunity was evaluated in its cleanest forms, which was what's equity beta, what's the liquidity and what's the cost of that and what's its leverage.
turns.zh: 私募是另一种生物。对某些私募市场和某些私募资产类别，TPA 很难做。我们作为通才打下的根基在于：每一个投资机会都在其最纯粹的形式下被评估，也就是它的股票贝塔、流动性、成本、杠杆各是多少。

turns.en: Not necessarily do we want an India VC manager or do we want a X type of manager? It was very little bucket filling. It was a bottom sub, first principle so what an investment was.
turns.zh: 而不是说，我们要不要一个印度 VC 管理人，或者要不要某一类型的管理人。几乎没有凑数式的填桶。它是自下而上、从一笔投资的第一性原理出发的。

turns.en: How did your role and responsibilities evolve over time? Today I spend most of my time on a private portfolio. We had a CEO transition about Midway in my nine year career here.
turns.zh: 你的角色和职责随时间是如何演变的？如今我把大部分时间花在私募组合上。在我在这儿的九年职业生涯中，大约在中间时经历过一次 CEO 交接。

turns.en: The portfolio construction piece had been less attended to. We had very little venture in the portfolio, especially compared to our peers. We also needed to diversify the bio portfolio a lot.
turns.zh: 组合构建这一块之前关注得较少。我们组合里的风投（venture）很少，尤其和同行相比。我们也需要把收购（buyout）组合大幅多元化。

turns.en: On top of adding things like growth equity, we evolved into a more specialist concept on the senior team. Two of us took over privates, two took over publics.
turns.zh: 除了加入成长型股权之类的东西，我们在高级团队上演变出了更偏专才（specialist）的模式——我们两人接手私募，两人接手公开市场。

turns.en: I moved to San Francisco to the Bay Area near Palo Alto. I moved there four years ago. Was this for love also? Maybe for the love of my children, but...
turns.zh: 我搬到了旧金山、搬到 Palo Alto 附近的湾区，四年前搬过去的。这也是为了爱情吗？也许是为了我爱孩子们的那种爱，不过……

turns.en: There you go. Also for the love of technology, I was fascinated with this whole area. We'd love to dive into two of the things that you mentioned in particular, the first being the CEO-CIO transition.
turns.zh: 对嘛。也是为了对科技的热爱，我迷上了这一整片区域。我们很想深入你提到的两件事，第一是这次 CEO-CIO 的交接。

turns.en: Curious what that was like from your vantage point as someone on the team and the organization is going through that transition? Uncertainty is always tough for anybody.
turns.zh: 很好奇，作为团队中正在经历这次交接的一员，从你的视角看那是什么滋味？不确定性对任何人来说都很难熬。

turns.en: You don't know who's gonna come in next. You don't know what the next 10 years is gonna look like. Also thinking about the possibility that somebody would come in and we would learn a lot from a new framework.
turns.zh: 你不知道下一个进来的人是谁，不知道未来 10 年会是什么样子。同时也在想这样一种可能性：某个新的人进来，我们会从一套新框架里学到很多。

turns.en: When I would sell people's, if you spend a lot of time in one place, you know a maelstrom, but that's the only maelstrom that you know. For me, it was a way to potentially learn a new maelstrom that I might really like.
turns.zh: 我常跟人这么说：如果你在一个地方待了很久，你熟悉一个漩涡（maelstrom），但那只是你唯一认识的漩涡。对我来说，那是一个可能去学一个新漩涡、而我也许会非常喜欢的机会。

turns.en: Peter is wonderful and I learned so much from him. It was one style of investing. I was one person and one type of team. I thought it'd be really interesting in some ways to learn from a different perspective as well.
turns.zh: Peter 非常好，我从他身上学到很多。那是一种投资风格，一个人、一种团队。我觉得从另一个视角去学，在某些方面会很有意思。

turns.en: It is scary. There are some good things in there. Obviously, I had known Kim because she had responded to my cool cool figures. Sarah and Dippity had its finest there, full circle.
turns.zh: 它确实吓人，但也有好的东西。显然我认识 Kim，因为她当年回复过我的陌生电话，兜了个圈子又回来了。

turns.en: She's a big supporter of a lot of different LP initiatives, so we had interacted a lot in the intervening years. I had a lot of respect for her.
turns.zh: 她是很多不同 LP 倡议的大力支持者，所以在这些年间我们有过很多互动，我非常尊敬她。

turns.en: She came in, I always tell the story because it tells you how much I don't know, but when we didn't know who the CIO was to a few people, I said, I hope they don't take away this generalist thing because it's something I truly love.
turns.zh: 她进来时——我总会讲这个故事，因为它说明我有多少不知道的东西——当我们还不知道 CIO 是谁时，我跟几个人说，我希望他们别把这套通才的东西拿走，因为那是我真爱的东西。

turns.en: It's always been how I approach the LP world. And of course, one of the things that did happen was that I became a specialist versus a generalist.
turns.zh: 那一直是我面对 LP 世界的方式。而当然，最终发生的一件事是，我从通才变成了专才。

turns.en: It's still valuable when you're younger and you come in with a generalist mindset. You're able to compare cross asset classes. You're picking from a bigger universe.
turns.zh: 当你年轻、以通才心态入行时，这仍然很有价值。你能跨资产类别去比较，你在一个更大的宇宙里挑选。

turns.en: Some asset classes are not the right time or space. When Kim came in and made us specialists, I was nervous about the whole transition. I have learned so much from being a asset class specialist to some extent.
turns.zh: 有些资产类别并不是合适的时机或空间。当 Kim 进来、把我们变成专才时，我对整个转变是紧张的。但从某种程度上说，作为资产类别专才我也学到了很多。

turns.en: We still keep a lot of generalist heritage. We discuss every fun together. I can bring in a hedge fund or a long lay fund. The benefit to being a specialist for me a little bit later in life was that there was this element of portfolio construction that I had not appreciated.
turns.zh: 我们仍然保留了大量通才的传承——我们一起讨论每一笔交易，我可以带进一只对冲基金或一只长期多空（long/short）基金。对我而言，在人生稍晚成为专才的好处是：组合构建里有一个我之前未曾领会的维度。

turns.en: Planning, thinking through your tilts about researching different areas that you needed to inject into a portfolio. That was something that I had not had a ton of interaction with when I was a generalist.
turns.zh: 做规划，思考你的倾斜，研究你需要注入组合的不同领域。那是我当通才时接触不多的东西。

turns.en: A little bit more in the family office because it was one big portfolio divided into many different portfolios for different trusts and accounts.
turns.zh: 在家族办公室会多一些，因为那是一个大组合，被拆成给不同信托和账户的许多子组合。

turns.en: Wasn't something that I thought that much about. In the last four years, when I've spent most of my time in private, that's been an area that I've had a ton of growth in, talking to different people.
turns.zh: 但那不是我思考得太多的东西。在过去四年里，当我把大部分时间花在私募上之后，那成了我成长非常多的一个领域，我和不同的人交流。

turns.en: During that process, when you know the team structure is changing to a specialist model, you're nervous about it. What do you do about being nervous?
turns.zh: 在那个过程中，当你意识到团队结构要转向专才模式、你对此感到紧张时，你怎么对待那份紧张？

turns.en: Do you articulate those nerves and potentially those reservations? Or do you follow your marching orders because that's the new direction of the organization?
turns.zh: 你会把那种紧张、乃至那些保留意见说出来吗？还是照着命令行事，因为那是组织的新方向？

turns.en: One thing that was comforting was that we never lost our general's heritage. Kim was very specific that it was not the intention. It was more that we kept what we had and there was an overlay of something that was going to be additive versus taking something away.
turns.zh: 让人宽慰的一点是，我们从未丢掉通才的传承。Kim 很明确地说那不是本意，更多的是一种：我们保留已有的，再叠加一层只会做加法、而非拿走什么的东西。

turns.en: That was a great form of communication from her. Speaks a lot to how she thinks and communicates things within the team. Everything that we do is never authoritative from above.
turns.zh: 那是她一种很好的沟通方式，也很能说明她如何在团队里思考和传达事情。我们做的任何事，从来不是自上而下的硬性命令。

turns.en: She does a really good job of inciting discussion, getting points be across that might be different from what the directive is, and then including them and how it's executed.
turns.zh: 她很擅长引发讨论，让一些可能与指令不同的观点表达出来，然后在执行时把它们纳入进去。

turns.en: Today, I don't think that I've lost anything. I've gained a ton. That was the narrative that the story played out exactly as it did. When you said it was changing from a generalist team to a specialist team, that wasn't how I thought about it.
turns.zh: 如今，我不觉得自己失去了什么，我收获了很多。那是这个故事实际展开的方式。你说从通才团队变成专才团队时，那并不是我当时的理解方式。

turns.en: It wasn't how it played out. It's a little bit of false economies up my head. We're going to take a quick break in the action to tell you about Brookfield.
turns.zh: 那也不是事情实际展开的样子，那有点是我脑子里错误的权衡。我们来在中途插一段，给你讲讲 Brookfield。

turns.en: Brookfield invests in the thing behind the thing behind the next big thing. Their focus across infrastructure, energy, real estate, private equity, and credit is helping to build the backbone of the global economy.
turns.zh: Brookfield 投资于那个大事件背后的、背后的东西。他们在基础设施、能源、房地产、私募股权和信贷上的布局，正在帮助构建全球经济的骨架。

turns.en: Brookfield combines deep operational expertise with disciplined long-term investing, uncovering value, and partnering alongside clients to shape tomorrow's economy today.
turns.zh: Brookfield 把深厚的运营专长与纪律严明的长期投资相结合，发现价值，与客户并肩合作，在今天塑造明天的经济。

turns.en: Invest in the businesses that shape tomorrow. Learn how you can own what's next at Brookfield.com slash own. This is not an offer to sell or investment advice.
turns.zh: 投资于那些塑造明天的企业。前往 Brookfield.com/own，了解你如何拥有下一个机遇。这不是出售要约，也不构成投资建议。

turns.en: Investing involves risk, including the loss of capital. And now, back to the show. Today, how do you spend your time? If I think about my time pie chart, it changes every week.
turns.zh: 投资涉及风险，包括损失本金。现在，回到节目。今天你怎么分配你的时间？要说我的时间饼图，它每周都在变。

turns.en: Probably 25% of my time with existing managers. Another 25% of my time meeting new managers. The last pieces are thinking about the portfolio, trying to figure out which areas of new research there is.
turns.zh: 大概 25% 花在现有的管理人上，另外 25% 花在会见新的管理人。剩下的部分是思考组合，试着找出有哪些新的研究领域。

turns.en: We've been doing a lot of co-invest this year. The rest of the time, camp includes us in a lot of risk management and portfolio decisions. I spent a lot of my time in that as well, and team management.
turns.zh: 今年我们做了很多 co-invest（联合投资）。其余时间还包括大量风险管理和组合决策，我在那些上也花了很多时间，还有团队管理。

turns.en: That's the last 25% or so. Let's dive into each of those a little bit. Within manager selection, let's start there. For new managers, when do you decide to get involved in a new manager diligence process?
turns.zh: 那大概就是最后 25% 左右。我们分别深入聊聊。管理人选择，就从这里开始。对新管理人，你什么时候决定投入一个新管理人的尽调流程？

turns.en: The nice thing about having such a small team, we have 15 people on the investment side, is that we are transparent and communicative. Almost from the beginning, most people know what we're working on individually.
turns.zh: 团队小的好处——我们投资端只有 15 个人——是我们透明、爱沟通。几乎从一开始，每个人各自在做什么，大家彼此都清楚。

turns.en: As somebody who's in California, and as somebody who has spent a lot of time in privates, even when it's pretty early on, someone would flag to me, hey, I'm talking to this person.
turns.zh: 作为身在加州、又花大量时间在私募上的人，即便还非常早期，也会有人跟我打个招呼：嘿，我在和这个人聊。

turns.en: Have you met them before? Hopefully you made it into my notes consolidator. Early on, I would have a flag whether we're talking to somebody, and if I have a strong opinion there, I would say something.
turns.zh: 你见过他吗？希望我的笔记系统里有记录。很早我就会有一个提示，知道我们在和谁谈，如果我对此有强烈看法，我会说出来。

turns.en: If not, the team can take several meetings before I, or somebody else who's on the private side, step in. We have a standard process, which is similar to what I had a cat it in, where we do a one-pager for managers that we meet, and we socialize it with the team.
turns.zh: 如果没有，团队可以先开几次会，之后才由我或私募侧的其他人介入。我们有一套标准流程，和以前 Camden 那套类似：为我们见到的管理人写一页纸（one-pager），然后和团队一起过一遍。

turns.en: And that's typically when it's a little bit more than a flicker of interest. That's either a sector or a type of investment that we want to discuss with the team, or a manager that we think is interesting.
turns.zh: 那通常是在兴趣稍微多一点点的火花时——要么是我们想和团队讨论的某个行业或某类投资，要么是我们觉得有意思的某位管理人。

turns.en: We do a one-pager there, the team will comment on it. If it's still interesting for that smaller group that we call the deal team and moves on to the five-pager, where we get to the key questions for every investment, I belong to the school where I believe that there's probably five things unique to every investment that will make or break the deal or make or break the returns.
turns.zh: 在那里我们先做一页纸，团队会评论。如果对我们称为 deal team 的那个小圈子来说仍然有意思，就进入五页纸（five-pager），那里会触及每笔投资的关键问题。我信奉这样一种观点：每笔投资大概都有五件独特的东西，会决定这笔交易或这组回报的成败。

turns.en: We try to get to those questions in a five-pager. We deliberate them in an intensive way during that time. The final thing is investment proposal.
turns.zh: 我们试图在五页纸里问到那些问题，在那段时间里高强度地论证它们。最后一步是投资提案（investment proposal）。

turns.en: By the time it gets to investment proposal, it's usually pretty baked, and it answers a lot of the questions that were raised within the first two processes.
turns.zh: 到投资提案这一步时，通常已经很成熟，并且回答了前两个流程里提出的很多问题。

turns.en: I usually am quite involved during the five-pager process, at least, sometimes not during the one-pager, though. If you can think of a recent example where you made a commitment to a new manager that was not in the portfolio, what were your specific touchpoints and your specific involvement in that investment?
turns.zh: 我通常至少在五页纸流程里深度参与，有时在一页纸阶段则不然。你能不能想一个最近的例子，你向一个原本不在组合里的新管理人做了出资承诺，你在那个投资里具体的接触点和参与程度是怎样的？

turns.en: I'm usually pretty involved. Good ideas can come from anywhere. Nobody in the team is monopoly on good ideas. I would hope that having a lot of mistakes in the past that I have some judgment, that's where I mostly come in.
turns.zh: 我通常参与度挺高。好主意可以来自任何地方，团队里没有人对好主意有垄断权。我希望凭过去犯过的很多错，我多少有点判断力，那主要是我发挥作用的地方。

turns.en: Let's say somebody else brings a manager in that he or she thinks is super interesting. I would typically meet them probably in a second time.
turns.zh: 比如说另一位带进来一位他/她觉得非常有意思的管理人，我通常大概会在第二次会面时见他们。

turns.en: If we have a good conversation, then we proceed with the questions that we want to answer. That's where the person who's working on it with me, we iterate a lot on what those questions are.
turns.zh: 如果我们谈得不错，就接着推进我们想回答的那些问题。在那儿，和我一起跟这笔投资的同事会在这些问题上反复迭代。

turns.en: We start calling people. The word streams are usually pretty standard. At this point, I probably get the most involved at the what other questions that we need to answer when we are doing references.
turns.zh: 我们开始打电话。那些话术流程通常相当固定。到这一步，我最多参与的是在背景调查（references）时我们还需要回答哪些问题。

turns.en: I like to do optimist references. We tend to do a lot of that. That's where a network comes in helpful because people are willing to tell you the truth about what you're asking them.
turns.zh: 我喜欢做乐观背调（optimist references），我们倾向于多做这类。那里正是网络帮上忙的地方，因为人们愿意就你问的告诉你真相。

turns.en: Off-list references are easier said than done. What are some tips and tricks that you have of answering the questions that you need answered?
turns.zh: 非名单背调（off-list references）是说起来容易做起来难。你有什么技巧和窍门来回答你需要回答的问题？

turns.en: Have you invested in a really strong network? Has been helpful? People have concentrated circles of how much they tell people. Did you call somebody as a cold call as an off-list reference and you don't know them, you don't have any connectivity with them?
turns.zh: 你有没有投资建立一个很强的网络？很有帮助。人们愿意向人透露多少，是有圈子的。你是作为一个非名单背调对象去打的陌生电话、你根本不认识对方、和对方没有任何连接吗？

turns.en: It's very little chance somebody's going to tell you something interesting. But if you have a warm introduction or somebody that you already know, which is 70% of the time that's the case, or somebody that you know who works in the industry and knows the reputation of whoever you're calling about, that's a different off-list reference.
turns.zh: 那种情况下，有人告诉你有价值信息的几率很小。但如果你有暖介绍、或一个你已经认识的人——大约 70% 的情况是这种——或者一个你认识的、在行业里、了解你要打的那个人的名声的人，那就是另一种非名单背调。

turns.en: It tends to be quite valuable. We have absolutely said no to funds because of an off-list reference that we got that was negative and was corroborated by others.
turns.zh: 它往往相当有价值。我们确实因为一次负面的、并被其他人佐证的非名单背调，而对某只基金说了'不'。

turns.en: Let's look at a counter example. You mentioned the other half of your time in manager selection is with existing managers. Curious when you decide that you might need to exit a manager relationship.
turns.zh: 我们来看一个反例。你提到你在管理人选择上另一半时间是花在现有管理人上。很好奇，你什么时候决定可能需要退出与某位管理人的关系。

turns.en: Breakups are the hardest thing in this industry. I have to do them on days that I know I can be sad. It is tough, especially in a private site when you spend a lot of time with somebody and you expect to be with them for 10 years.
turns.zh: 分手是这个行业里最难的事。我不得不在知道自己可以难过的那种日子去做。这很难，尤其是在私募那一侧，你和某人相处了很多年，你本来指望和他们待上 10 年。

turns.en: That's hopefully the minimum of how much time we are with the manager. Some of the mistakes that I've made in the past amongst many is when you stay on the bus for too long, that can be part of the biggest reasons that we break up with managers.
turns.zh: 那希望是我们和管理人相处的最短时间。我过去犯过的一些错误之一就是——在车上待得太久，这可能是我们和管理人分手的最大原因之一。

turns.en: We try to message that way in advance, so it's not a surprise. Nobody wants to hear about a breakup from a post-it note. Usually the biggest reason is the idea that we think that they're in a different strategy.
turns.zh: 我们试图提前很久就传达这个意思，让它不是一场意外。没人想从一张便利贴上得知分手的消息。通常最大的理由是：我们觉得他们已经在做另一套策略了。

turns.en: Fund size increases that go way beyond what we feel is appropriate for this strategy. That's a mathematical one. That's more of are you now searching for AUM versus returns?
turns.zh: 基金规模的增长远超我们认为对这套策略合适的范围。那是一个数学层面的问题，更像是在问：你现在追求的是 AUM 还是回报？

turns.en: Sometimes we accept that. Sometimes even when managers triple, double their front sizes, it's not an unequivocal no. We need to analyze and see if we think it's still appropriate for this strategy.
turns.zh: 有时我们能接受。有时即便管理人把基金规模翻两倍、翻三倍，也不是一个斩钉截铁的'不'，我们需要分析，看我们是否认为对这套策略仍然合适。

turns.en: The second reason is sometimes we feel that the managed life cycle is toward the end. You have a lot of turnover. You have carry that's allocated in ways that we don't think reflects the talent that's in your organization.
turns.zh: 第二个理由是，有时我们觉得这家管理人的生命周期已接近尾声。人员大量流动，carry 的分配方式在我们看来并不反映你们组织里的真才实学。

turns.en: That's more of a narrative. That's a story around how we feel the future is gonna be and nothing to do with their returns. The last reason and hopefully the reason that happens to least is if we feel that the manager, this is a red flag reason, has sent something to us that was not accurate.
turns.zh: 那更像是一种叙事，一个关于我们觉得未来会怎样的故事，和他们的回报无关。最后一个理由——希望它最少发生——如果我们觉得那位管理人（这是一个红旗理由）给了我们一些不准确的表述。

turns.en: Honesty and transparency and trusting your manager is such an important piece of this relationship. That is absolutely a reason that we would break up with someone.
turns.zh: 诚实、透明、信任你的管理人，是这段关系里极其重要的一部分。那绝对是我们分手的一个理由。

turns.en: How much of exit decisions are based on some of the portfolio characteristics on your side versus characteristics from the manager, especially today where there's lots of market construct changes happening on both the public and the private side?
turns.zh: 退出决定有多大比例是基于你这侧的组合特征，而不是来自管理人的特征，尤其是在今天公开和私募两侧都在发生很多市场结构性变化的时候？

turns.en: There are portfolio construction decisions that determine how much we allocate to a manager, how many managers we allocate to and whether we would add to a new manager.
turns.zh: 有一些组合构建层面的决策，决定我们给一位管理人配置多少、给多少位管理人配置、以及是否增加一位新管理人。

turns.en: Also the construction is huge. Sometimes when you overload and too many managers in one sector that can happen, it usually comes with a much bigger portfolio review.
turns.zh: 构建也很重要。有时当你在某个行业上过于拥挤、管理人太多——这种情况会发生——它通常伴随一次更大范围的组合审视。

turns.en: When that happens, it happens during a time that we have decided to make a bigger change to our portfolio. Sometimes we will trim on the margin if we have too many tech file managers.
turns.zh: 当那种情况发生时，是在我们已经决定对组合做一次更大改动的时刻。有时我们会在边际上缩减，如果我们科技赛道的管理人太多的话。

turns.en: Maybe we won't add a bunch more. Maybe marginally we can trim some or we can trim our commitments. We try to manage it like that versus on a dime, say no to a relationship that we think very highly of or care a lot about.
turns.zh: 也许我们不会再加一大批。也许在边际上我们可以缩减一些，或者缩减我们的承诺。我们试着这样管理，而不是临时说'不'、拒绝一段我们非常看好、非常在意的关系。

turns.en: As your role has evolved over nine years, how and when have you delegated certain components of manager relationship for an existing manager or new manager underwriting as you've progressed in your existing role?
turns.zh: 随着你的角色在九年间演变，在你现有职位上一步步前进的过程中，你是如何、以及何时把某位现有管理人或新管理人 underwriting 的某些环节委派出去的？

turns.en: When you move from a generalist model where manager selection is your job and a lot of your job, you are involved in every single thing with that manager, including negotiating legals.
turns.zh: 当你从一种通才模式——在那里管理人选择就是你工作的一大块——转出来时，你参与那位管理人的一切，包括谈判法律条款。

turns.en: All the desk work as a generalist, I was in Excel looking at things. These things are harder to do as a portfolio constructor because there's just not enough hours in the day.
turns.zh: 作为通才时所有案头工作，我在 Excel 里看各种东西。作为组合构建者这些就更难做了，因为一天没有那么多小时。

turns.en: When we decided to go more to the deal team format, which is similar to private equity where you have somebody who is driving and then somebody else who's underwriting, we split it with clean lines.
turns.zh: 当我们决定更转向 deal team 模式——类似私募股权，有一个人在牵头、另一个人在做 underwriting——我们用清晰的界限把它分开。

turns.en: It would be more the relationship piece of things and then the underwriting piece of things. Somebody else has a big responsibility to underwrite the investment.
turns.zh: 一方面更多是关系的部分，另一方面是 underwriting 的部分。另一个人承担起对这笔投资做 underwriting 的重大责任。

turns.en: Those are probably the biggest responsibilities that I left behind when we decided to move to more a specialist model, not to say that I am not looking cut to data because clearly you need to make a decision.
turns.zh: 那些大概是我们决定转向更专才模式时，我放下的最大责任；但这并不是说我不再去看数据，因为你显然要做决策。

turns.en: There's a lot of questions that need to be answered. We do have stock analysis. The most important things and the things that drive investment decisions are the creativity around how you answer some of these questions.
turns.zh: 有很多问题需要回答。我们确实有个股分析。最重要的、驱动投资决策的东西，是围绕如何回答某些问题的创造力。

turns.en: It dovetails nicely into the next bucket of your existing responsibilities being that portfolio construction piece. It's hard not to discuss the current market environment as it relates to portfolio construction.
turns.zh: 这很自然地接上了你现有职责的下一个板块——组合构建这一块。很难不把当前的市场环境摆到组合构建的语境里来谈。

turns.en: The first place to start on that front is liquidity. What is your approach to the liquidity dynamics of private markets where companies are staying private for longer?
turns.zh: 在这方面第一个要谈的是流动性。面对私募市场的流动性动态——公司更长时间保持私有——你是什么思路？

turns.en: There's less distributions on the back end. There's less exits on the back end. How have you approached all of those dynamics from a portfolio construction perspective?
turns.zh: 后端分配变少了，后端的退出也变少了。从组合构建的视角，你是怎么看待所有这些动态的？

turns.en: With regard to your point about private companies staying private longer, the attractiveness of private markets is still there. We believe in it.
turns.zh: 就你提到的私募公司更长期私有化这一点，私募市场的吸引力依然存在，我们相信它。

turns.en: We're growing it. On the liquidity point, it's a little different for us because I mentioned in the beginning, we have very little venture coming into late 20s.
turns.zh: 我们在增长它。关于流动性这一点，对我们来说有点不同，因为我一开始说过，我们直到 20 年代后期才进来的风投很少。

turns.en: We don't have a huge illiquid portfolio and we have a comfortable amount of unfunded today. We have room to grow, especially as public markets have outrun private markets.
turns.zh: 我们并没有一个庞大的非流动组合，我们今天有一笔舒适的未注资额（unfunded）。我们还有增长的空间，尤其是在公开市场跑赢私募市场之后。

turns.en: I don't want to switch it anytime, but it's been a significant run for public markets. The liquidity piece we are always watching, but at this point, we have root place among fence versus defense.
turns.zh: 我不想轻易转变，但公开市场已经经历了一波可观的行情。流动性这一点我们一直在盯，但在当下，我们更像是进攻而非防守。

turns.en: The last thing, talking about market environment, there's some insanity out there. One of the ways that we've managed that is in secure diversification.
turns.zh: 最后一点，谈市场环境，外面有些疯狂。我们管理它的方式之一，是 vintage 分散化（vintage diversification）。

turns.en: This is the most crucial time to exercise that. Why is that? Venture diversification has always been an important venture. This year in particular, with so many funds raising, with so many companies raising, at valuations that are multiples of what they just graced about six months ago, we don't want to put all your eggs in a 2026 bucket where people feel good about AI.
turns.zh: 现在是行使这一点最关键的时机。为什么？风投的 vintage 分散化一直很重要。尤其是今年，有那么多基金在募集、那么多公司在募资——那些估值是他们大约六个月前融资价的好几倍——我们不想把所有鸡蛋都放进 2026 年这个桶里，那时人们对 AI 都很看好。

turns.en: There are going to be fortunes made in this vintage. You want to be part of the 27 vintage as well. Maybe the next video is not going to be built until 2028.
turns.zh: 这个 vintage 里会有人赚到巨额财富。你也想参与到 2027 年的 vintage 里。也许下一个伟大的公司要到 2028 年才会被打造出来。

turns.en: Vintage or diversification, particularly in this time and moment, is something that we're watching. What are some of the other characteristics in addition to vintage or diversification that inform your portfolio construction in today's environment?
turns.zh: vintage 分散化，尤其在此时此刻，是我们一直在关注的一点。除了 vintage 分散化，在当前环境下还有哪些特征会影响你的组合构建？

turns.en: We think about things as tilts. What are the tilts that we're comfortable with? We categorize them into things like geography. Right now, our US portfolio, our US venture portfolio, our US bio portfolios, portfolio in general, is tilted.
turns.zh: 我们把各种东西看作倾斜（tilt）。我们乐意承受哪些倾斜？我们按地域等类别来划分。现在，我们的美国组合、我们的美国风投组合、美国生物（bio）组合、以及整体组合，都是有倾斜的。

turns.en: Are we okay with that? We had a lot of discussions about American exceptionalism a few years ago. Still do. There's a lot of questions around what bets are you taking in every single asset class, then on the portfolio, and you roll it up to the portfolio.
turns.zh: 我们对此 OK 吗？几年前我们就美国例外论（American exceptionalism）有很多讨论，现在也还在讨论。围绕你在每个资产类别里下的是什么注、然后在组合层面汇总上去，有很多问题。

turns.en: GEO is one of them, early glitch versus late stage. It's one of them. There's in BC, the question of specialists versus generals as well. A lot of the BC that we came in with in the 2020s was biotech.
turns.zh: 地域是其中之一，早期阶段 vs 后期阶段也是其中之一。在 VC 里，还有专才 vs 通才的问题。我们在 2020 年代进来时的很多 VC 是 biotech（生物科技）。

turns.en: That's been a small part of our BC portfolio today, so we neglect tech versus biotech. That's an area that you need to also pay attention to.
turns.zh: 那如今在我们 VC 组合里只占很小一部分，所以在科技与生物科技之间我们有所取舍。这也是你需要留意的一个领域。

turns.en: What are the risks that you consider when you put together the private portfolio? The biggest one, particularly for biob, is higher interest rates.
turns.zh: 你在搭建私募组合时会考虑哪些风险？最大的一个，尤其是对收购（buyout）而言，是更高的利率。

turns.en: It makes the math different. It makes the growth of the companies more important. Being able to expand margins a lot more important. Do private agree firms that we look at have the ability to generate that value today?
turns.zh: 它让数学变了，让公司的增长变得更重要，让扩大利润率的能力重要得多。我们考察的那些私募股权机构，今天有没有能力创造那种价值？

turns.en: That's a big question for us. The existence of higher interest rates is a risk for a lot of firms to think about. The second risk is the concentration of bets that we have in some parts of our portfolio.
turns.zh: 那对我们是个大问题。更高利率的存在，是很多机构要思考的风险。第二个风险是我们在组合某些部分的下注集中度。

turns.en: With regard to BC, we have a lot of companies that a lot of people have invested in. Some of them are spectacular companies and generational companies.
turns.zh: 说到 VC，我们投了很多别人也投了很多的公司。其中一些是了不起的公司、是世代级的公司。

turns.en: Happy to have those in our portfolio. But I also worry a little bit about group think, the idea that there's a concentration in a bet that also has underlying risks.
turns.zh: 把它们放进组合我们很高兴。但我也对群体思维（groupthink）有一点担忧——那种在某个同样埋藏着底层风险的下注上过度集中的念头。

turns.en: What do you do about each of those? On the piece of higher interest rates, we spent a lot more time re-underwriting on matters today. One, to make sure that they are on the forefront and understand the dynamics of how the world's changing.
turns.zh: 对这些你分别怎么做？就更高利率这一块，我们今天花更多时间对管理人重新做 underwriting，一是确保他们站在最前沿、理解世界变化的动态。

turns.en: Your standard Valley Creation Bridge, there's the leverage piece of it, there's the operating margins and growth piece of it, there's the multiple expansion piece of it.
turns.zh: 你标准的价值创造桥（value creation bridge）里，有杠杆那一块，有经营利润率和增长那一块，有倍数扩张那一块。

turns.en: We like firms that have proven a lot of value in the operating piece of it. That idea of how do you replicate your success or your operating playbook is particularly important today for buyouts.
turns.zh: 我们喜欢那些在经营那一块证明了大量价值的机构。在收购（buyout）上，'你怎么复制你的成功、复制你的经营打法'这个理念尤其重要。

turns.en: For venture and the concentration of bets, a lot of it's understanding what's in your portfolio. The ability to do that on the part of our team is great.
turns.zh: 对风投和下注集中度，很多在于理解你组合里有什么。我们团队在这方面做得很好。

turns.en: There is the judgment call of, do you want to add to some of those companies or do you feel that you're over levers? Venture is inherently one of those asset classes.
turns.zh: 里面有一个判断：你是想加码其中一些公司，还是觉得你已经过度加杠杆（over-levered）？风投本身就是那种资产类别之一。

turns.en: Higher is high reward, it's equity seeking. Venture is doing what it should do. It's going after great companies. There are other parts of our portfolio where even within the private's portfolio and not extending into hedge funds and other types of diversifiers.
turns.zh: 风投天然高风险高回报、追逐股权，它正在做它该做的事——去投那些伟大的公司。我们组合里还有其他部分，即使在私募组合之内、而不延伸进对冲基金和其他类型的分散化工具时也一样。

turns.en: A buyout portfolio, we try to be diversified. We're not just doing tech buyouts. We also have a healthy and growing amount of the high asset, low obsolescence type strategies, the hail strategies, love that name.
turns.zh: 在收购组合上，我们力求分散。我们不只是做科技收购。我们也持有一份健康且在增长的、高资产、低淘汰（low obsolescence）类型的策略，就是所谓的 HAIL 策略，我很喜欢这个名字。

turns.en: That was deliberate. So five years ago, we set out to build a portfolio that was durable in a buyout site. That does act as a buffer to some of the bets that we feel are concentrated.
turns.zh: 那是刻意为之。五年前，我们着手去搭建一个在收购端足够耐用的组合。它确实对我们觉得过于集中的某些下注起到了缓冲作用。

turns.en: On the buyout front, where have you found pockets of operational edge? Specialists can be helpful there when you have a healthcare specialist firm, when you have a consumer specialist firm that only does certain types of strategies.
turns.zh: 在收购这一块，你在哪些地方找到了运营上的优势（operational edge）？专才在那里会有帮助——当你有一家医疗专才机构、一家只做某些类型策略的消费专才机构时。

turns.en: You get good at executing the same playbook. You've seen a lot of the same movie before. You know all the executives in that arena. You know their reputations by gravitating towards that mindset, this value at when you can speak the same language and you know something well.
turns.zh: 你会擅长执行同一套打法，你已经看过很多遍同样的电影，你认识那个领域里所有的管理层，你知道他们的名声。转向那种心态，就是在你能说同一种语言、对某样东西了如指掌时去下注。

turns.en: That's one area that is interesting. The buy and build strategies have been something that people have been talking about for a few years now.
turns.zh: 那是一个有意思的方向。buy-and-build（收购整合）策略，人们已经谈了好几年了。

turns.en: People say to the dream buy and build. I always have a lot of follow up questions because it's such a difficult strategy to execute. Integration of anything is hard.
turns.zh: 人们说'去做那个梦想般的 buy-and-build'。我总是有很多追问，因为那是极难执行的策略，整合任何东西都很难。

turns.en: Being able to successfully strategically put together a company, integrate that and create value out of one plus one equals three is difficult to do.
turns.zh: 能够成功地把一家公司战略性地拼装起来、把它整合好、从 1+1=3 中创造价值，是一件很难做到的事。

turns.en: People who do it well can generate exceptional results. We've seen our specialists and generalist firms do a good job there. It requires good resources and a little bit of a unique way of thinking of how to build a business.
turns.zh: 把它做好的人能产出非凡的成果。我们见过专才机构和通才机构在那里做得很好。它需要不错的资源，也需要一点如何构建一门生意的独特思路。

turns.en: I wanna shift to the last bucket of your time allocation being on team. You mentioning that being an increasing responsibility especially since Kim has been on as CEO and CIO.
turns.zh: 我想转到你时间分配的最后一个板块——团队。你提到这尤其在 Kim 出任 CEO 兼 CIO 之后成了一项日益增重的责任。

turns.en: What are the types of initiatives that you own on the team front? There are 15 people on the investment team. SMGs, we all individually have people who report directly to us.
turns.zh: 在团队这块，你负责哪些类型的举措？投资团队有 15 个人，作为 MD，我们每个人各自都有直接汇报给我们的人。

turns.en: We're responsible for their coaching and mentorship. Maybe because I have a bit of my mom's heritage, I do just spend a lot of time getting to know people, try and understand what makes them tick.
turns.zh: 我们要负责他们的辅导（coaching）和 mentoring。也许是因为我身上有点妈妈的传承，我真的花很多时间去了解人，试着理解他们是被什么驱动的。

turns.en: That's the most important thing about mentoring a team. People have goals, people with strengths and weaknesses. As somebody who has a few more years on them, it's interesting to be able to help them leverage their strengths and think about what they can do a little bit better.
turns.zh: 那是带团队最重要的一点。人有目标，人有长处和短处。作为一个多干几年的人，能够帮助他们发挥所长、思考哪里能做得更好，是很有意思的。

turns.en: The formal responsibilities are one piece of what any organization can have. The execution of it is more important. The mindset of let's give people feedback in a way that is constructive.
turns.zh: 正式的职责是任何组织都可能具备的一块，但更重要的是它的执行，是那种'让我们以建设性的方式给人反馈'的心态。

turns.en: Let's tell people if they are doing something that is probably not good for us and probably not good for their careers. The social contract, how do you be a good mentor and coach?
turns.zh: 让我们在有人做了大概对我们不好、也对他们职业不好的事时告诉他们。那份社会契约——你怎么当一个好导师、好教练？

turns.en: The team is so small that I just don't think that matters as much as the mindset that has been set up and the cultural mindset of talking a lot to your team members.
turns.zh: 团队这么小，我真的觉得那些形式不重要——重要的是已经立起来的心态，以及那种文化心态：多和你的团队成员沟通。

turns.en: The first thing I always tell people, a lot of analysts, they come in from the investment banking. When I was in the investment banking, you didn't talk to AMD, that's true.
turns.zh: 我总告诉新人的第一件事是：很多分析师是从投行来的。我当年在投行时，你是不跟 MD 聊的，那是真的。

turns.en: They just sat there and made their calls. It's not that kind of organization. You can teamspeak anytime, your memes, anything that you think about.
turns.zh: 他们就坐在那儿打他们的电话。我们不是那种组织，你可以随时开 Teams 会议，聊你的想法、你想的任何东西。

turns.en: You have this formal construct of review and of having direct reports, and then you also have a more informal construct of having conversations about what is the culture of the organization.
turns.zh: 你有这种正式的架构——定期 review、带直接下属，然后你也有一个更非正式的架构——去谈论这个组织的文化是什么。

turns.en: What if someone doesn't vibe with either of those? You've identified them as probably not a good fit in the long term. How do you manage that from your seat?
turns.zh: 如果某个人和这两种都不契合怎么办？你已经认定他们长期大概不是好人选，你怎么从你的位置去处理？

turns.en: This is boring for my mom because she tells me this all the time. It's never the wrong person, it's the wrong job. People have different motivations, they've got different things.
turns.zh: 这会让我妈妈听得腻味，因为她老跟我讲这句话：从来不是错的人，而是错的工作。人有不同的动机，有各自不同的东西。

turns.en: Sometimes that's not the job they need or want. That's the biggest realization. You're not trying to put a square peg into a round hole. You put the square in a square.
turns.zh: 有时候那不是他们需要或想要的工作，那是最大的领悟。你不是在把一个方榫硬塞进圆孔，而是把方的放进方的。

turns.en: You try to help people figure out if they are not fitting. If something's going on where there's a lack of fit, is it because they want to do something else?
turns.zh: 你试着帮人们搞清楚：如果他们不合适——如果发生了某种不契合——是因为他们想做别的事吗？

turns.en: Is it because they culturally are different from a team mindset, which there are plenty of jobs where exceptionally intelligent people, which everybody in our team is, can go do that doesn't require you to be the biggest team member in the world.
turns.zh: 还是因为他们在文化上和团队心态不同？而有很多工作，才华横溢的人——我们团队里每个人都这么出色——都可以去做，那些工作并不要求你是世界上最好的'团队型'选手。

turns.en: There are people who go on and do different things. They find the job that is the right job for them. The other side of this question is, let's say via these constructs, you know an individual is going to be a high performer.
turns.zh: 有些人会转去做不同的事，找到那份对他们而言正确的工作。这个问题的另一面是：假设通过这些机制，你确知某个人会是高绩效者。

turns.en: You also know that career progression at a single organization is limited. You have 15 people, there are only a certain number of managing director seats.
turns.zh: 你也知道，在单一组织里的职业晋升是有限的。你有 15 个人，只有那么多 MD 席位。

turns.en: There's only one CIO seat. How do you manage that individual from your vantage point? There's titles and there's learning and responsibilities.
turns.zh: 只有一个 CIO 席位。你从你的视角怎么管理那个人？这里有头衔，也有学习和责任。

turns.en: The pyramid gets smaller at the top. It's not unique to us. It's not unique to our industry. The question is how do you keep high performers around?
turns.zh: 金字塔越往上越小。这不只是我们，也不只是我们这个行业。问题是怎么把高绩效者留下来？

turns.en: How do you leverage them? There's always natural succession in any organization. People leave to do different things at the senior end. People retire.
turns.zh: 你怎么发挥他们的作用？任何组织里都有自然的继替——在高级端人们离开去做别的事，人们退休。

turns.en: People decide to move laterally or upwards. There's some natural attrition that way that allows good talent to stay around. There's also the question of what do you do to inspire them during that time?
turns.zh: 有人决定横向或向上调动。有那种自然的流失，让好的人才得以留下。也有一个问题：在那段时间里你做什么来激励他们？

turns.en: What kind of responsibilities and learning curves can you give them? At a certain point in your career, that's what inspires you. If you're a curious person, which I think everybody in our team is, it's not necessarily when do I get the next title.
turns.zh: 你能给他们什么样的职责和学习曲线？在职业生涯的某个阶段，那才是激励你的东西。如果你是个好奇的人——我觉得我们团队里每个人都是——那未必是'我什么时候拿到下一个头衔'。

turns.en: It's when do I get some autonomy around certain things? When do I get the respect to do some independent things, satisfy my curiosity in a project that could be additive to the endowment?
turns.zh: 而是'我什么时候在某些事上获得一些自主权？我什么时候得到尊重去做一些独立的事，在一个可能对捐赠基金是加分的项目上满足我的好奇心？'

turns.en: There's always a lot of other things that you can do. What have you learned most from Kim as a manager and a leader? When Kim joined us, I called up a bunch of people and knew her.
turns.zh: 总有很多别的事你可以做。Kim 作为一位管理者、一位领导者，你从她身上学到最多的是什么？Kim 加入我们时，我给一批认识她的人打了电话。

turns.en: The one thing that stuck with me was one person told me, this is going to be the best experience of your professional career. I thought it was a wonderful reference on her.
turns.zh: 有一句让我印象很深：一个人跟我说，这将是你职业生涯里最好的经历。我觉得那是关于她的一句极好的评价。

turns.en: She's phenomenal. She is authentic, high intellectual house power IQ and IQ. What I found inspiring is the neuroplasticity that she has. She came into a structure that was different from the traditional endowment structure.
turns.zh: 她非常出色。她真实，有极高的智识诚实、强大的 IQ 和 EQ。我觉得鼓舞我的是她那种神经可塑性（neuroplasticity）。她进来时面对的是一个不同于传统捐赠基金的结构。

turns.en: She's managed to keep the pieces that were making it work, that were important to us, while also adding what was important to her. You have a lot of experience.
turns.zh: 她成功地保留了那些让这套结构运转、对我们重要的部分，同时加入了她认为重要的东西。你经验丰富。

turns.en: It's difficult to get yourself out of those ruts. Myself included, I have absolute biases that should be thrown out. What's so interesting about her is that she's always looking forward.
turns.zh: 要让自己跳出那些定式很难。包括我自己，我也有那种本应被扔掉的固有偏见。她有意思的地方在于，她总是向前看。

turns.en: She's always looking at why things have changed. Sometimes it has and it's the same movie. A lot of things change over time. She's moved along with that, specifically under people front, understanding people, leveraging the strengths and weaknesses.
turns.zh: 她总在看事物为什么变了。有时确实变了，有时又是同一部电影。很多东西随时间变化，她也随之向前——尤其在人这一块：理解人，用其所长、补其所短。

turns.en: She's exceptional at that, direct. That helps a lot too. When you can assess something, then you can communicate it in a way that is actionable and executable, that is the perfect type of thing you can do.
turns.zh: 她在这些方面出类拔萃，也很直接。那帮助很大。当你能够评估一件事，然后用一种可行动、可执行的方式把它传达出来，那就是你能做的最完美的事。

turns.en: How do you think about your own career progression in the seat you're in now? I really think the institution that I ended up for, when I got the job at Columbia, I remember telling the head hunter, I feel like I won the lottery.
turns.zh: 你怎么看待在现在这个位置上的自身职业进阶？我真的很感恩我最终落到的这个机构。拿到 Columbia 那份工作时，我记得我告诉那个猎头，我觉得自己中了彩票。

turns.en: I was so happy. This job is so interesting. It pushes my boundaries every single day. I could do this for a long time, having learned a lot from three phenomenal CIOs, Peter Holland, Tim Donahue, and Kim, all with different styles.
turns.zh: 我太开心了。这份工作太有意思，每一天都在推我的边界。我可以做很久——我从三位非凡的 CIO 那里学到很多：Peter Holland、Tim Donahue 和 Kim，风格各不相同。

turns.en: If at some point I find a place or a seat that allows me to contribute all those learnings, it would be interesting for me. I've never said no to change.
turns.zh: 如果有一天我找到一个地方或一个位置，能让我贡献出所有这些所学，那对我会很有意思。我从不对改变说不。

turns.en: This is a phenomenal seat and a great institution. What do you still want to learn before potentially assuming that role in the future? It feels like there's a new world order.
turns.zh: 这是一个很棒的位置、一所很棒的机构。在你将来可能承担那个角色之前，你还有什么想学的？感觉现在有一种新的世界秩序。

turns.en: There's the AI disruption. How do you invest through that? My kid calls it the olden days, which refers to anything that happened during my childhood.
turns.zh: 有 AI 的颠覆。你怎么穿越它去投资？我家孩子管它叫'老日子'（the olden days），指的是我童年时发生的任何事。

turns.en: The olden days of low interest rates. Certain things that we've been used to in the last 10, 20 years are not there anymore. The world's moving super fast.
turns.zh: 低利率的老日子。我们在过去 10、20 年习以为常的一些东西，已经不在那里了。世界变化极快。

turns.en: It's an interesting dynamic to consider. It's a lot to digest. How do you adapt to change that fast? How do you upgrade your brain to adapt to change?
turns.zh: 这是值得思考的有意思的动态，也是很多要消化的东西。你怎么应对那么快的变化？你怎么升级你的大脑去适应变化？

turns.en: The biggest thing I'm learning right now is that. How do you adapt to this changing condition? Manage selection. That's what I've been doing for most of my career, but you can always get better.
turns.zh: 我现在正在学的最大的就是那件事：你怎么适应这种不断变化的局面。管理人选择——那是我这辈子大半时间在做的事，但你总能做得更好。

turns.en: Portfolio construction. I'm learning new things every day. I'm making mistakes every day. How do you set culture? How do you make an organization better than when you were there?
turns.zh: 组合构建。我每天都在学新东西，每天也在犯错。你怎么设定文化？你怎么让一个组织比你来时更好？

turns.en: Building that and doing that is something I've been observing for a while. I learn every day on that. All right, Erlina, this has been a lot of fun.
turns.zh: 构建这些、做到这些，是我观察了一阵子的事，我每天在这一点上学。好，Erlina，这一期太有趣了。

turns.en: Let's turn to three rapid-fire closing questions. What is your favorite hobby or activity outside of working family? I give you the real answer, and then I'll give you the answer that I wish I were doing more.
turns.zh: 我们来做三个快问快答的收尾问题。在工作之外，你最喜欢的爱好或活动是什么？家庭——我给你真实的答案，然后给你那个我希望自己做得更多版本的答案。

turns.en: I read a lot. I read for 30 minutes to an hour every single day. It is my meditation to not disturb me at any point. That's probably the thing that I do the most consistently.
turns.zh: 我读很多书。我每天读 30 分钟到一个小时，那是我的冥想——任何时候别来打扰我。那大概是我做得最持之以恒的事。

turns.en: I love doing that. I only read fiction typically. Sometimes I'll put a nonfiction book in that I'm only read fiction. What did you read last?
turns.zh: 我很爱那样。我通常只读小说，偶尔会塞进一本非虚构，但我基本只读小说。你最近读了什么？

turns.en: I just finished Calambi Club by Catherine Sockert. Sometimes reread a lot of things. The thing that I reread the most is probably Three Body Problem.
turns.zh: 我刚读完 Catherine Sockert 的 Calambi Club。我有时重读很多东西，重读最多的可能是 Three Body Problem（《三体》）。

turns.en: I love that book. The final line that I was going to say was my husband and I did a lot of trip scuba diving. We've recently started that again because our kids are at a better age.
turns.zh: 我太爱那本书了。我本来要说的最后一句是：我先生和我过去做很多旅行式的水肺潜水（trip scuba diving），我们最近又开始了，因为孩子们到了更合适的年纪。

turns.en: There's something about being in this place that is much greater than yourself. What is your biggest investment pet peeve? I can't stand it when people are not intellectually honest.
turns.zh: 身处一个远比你自己宏大的地方，有一种特别的感觉。你最大的投资痛点是什么？我最受不了人们在智识上不诚实。

turns.en: I particularly don't like it when I hear anything like that in a team setting because I think that's where you should be intellectually honest.
turns.zh: 我尤其不喜欢在团队场合听到那样的东西，因为我觉得那正是你应该保持智识诚实的地方。

turns.en: I'm going to sell me something because you think I'm going to buy it. A lot of people are too focused on a short-term goal. They fail to realize that every time you say something that's a little bit more of an elaboration, it is discoverable.
turns.zh: 有人想卖给我一样东西，只因为你以为我会去买。很多人太盯着短期目标，没意识到每当你说的东西稍微夸张一点，它都是可被查证的。

turns.en: Then it makes the trust factor a little harder. People mistake identifying risks for a conviction and it goes to intellectual honesty. I've told my team a few times if you don't find awards, that's the thing that I would be upset about.
turns.zh: 这就让信任更难建立。人们常常把'识别风险'误当成'信念'，这又回到智识诚实。我跟团队说过好几次：如果你找不到风险，那反倒是我会恼火的事。

turns.en: We would accept awards because we need to accept them, but that's biggest pet peeve. Last one, what advice would you give a young allocator that you wish you had known earlier?
turns.zh: 我们得接受风险，因为我们需要去接受它们，但那才是我最大的痛点。最后一个：你会给一位年轻配置者什么建议——是你希望早点知道的？

turns.en: Doing something that scares you every day is a good one. In any job, when you're doing the same thing over and over again, you don't take risks in the sense that maybe you don't say something that you think should be said because you think it would be taken the wrong way or ask a question that you think you should be asked because you think it's dumb or reach out to that person that you don't reach out to
turns.zh: 每天都做一件让你害怕的事，这是个好建议。在任何工作里，当你日复一日做同样的事，你就不再冒险——也许是你不说那句你觉得该说的话，因为你怕被误解；不问那个你觉得该问的问题，因为你怕它很蠢；不去联系那个人，因为你……

turns.en: because you think they're too important. They don't have time for you. There's a little bit of that where within boundaries, don't be crazy about all that.
turns.zh: 因为你觉得对方太重要、没时间理你。多少有那么点这个意思。当然，一切要在界限之内，别太离谱。

turns.en: Doing something that scares you every day, what we're doing right now is the thing that scares me. Everyone hates public speaking. That's the only way to grow and it's important to challenge yourself to grow every day.
turns.zh: 每天做一件让你害怕的事——我们现在正在做的这件，就是让我害怕的事。人人都讨厌公开演讲。那是成长的唯一途径，每天都要挑战自己去成长，这很重要。

turns.en: Erlina, thank you so much for doing this. It was a total blast. Thanks for having me. Thanks for listening all the way to the end. If you made it this far, how about one ask for me?
turns.zh: Erlina，太感谢你这期来聊，真是痛快。谢谢邀请。感谢你们听到最后。如果你听到了这里，帮我一个忙如何？

turns.en: Tell one friend about the show. It's the best way to keep growing this incredible community. Thanks so much and until the next one, stay curious and keep compounding knowledge, relationships and capital a little bit at a time.
turns.zh: 把一个朋友介绍给这个节目。那是让这个了不起的社区不断成长最好的方式。非常感谢，我们下期再会——保持好奇，一点一点地让知识、关系和资本不断复利。
